title: Control Plane Weekly Field Sprint Wrapup - Oct 05 2027
content:
Weekly sync notes - Control Plane (routing / auth / quotas) — Field sprint wrapup (2027-10-05)

Attendees: Aisha Patel (lead), Marcus Liu, Elena Rodriguez, Samir Banerjee, Priya Shah, Alex Kim (guest), on-call SRE rotation.
Meeting length: 40m
Meeting type: weekly field sprint review + tactical handoff

1) Quick context / goals for this sprint week
- Primary focus: short-window routing fast-path for small payloads, quota fallback prototype, and resolving auth token expiry regressions observed in the week.
- Secondary: tighten config schema validation for route-to-pool assignments; polish canary gating for Dedicated pool rollouts.

2) Routing fast-path experiment (Marcus)
- What we ran: small-payload route that bypasses full router lookup and uses cached pool mapping + prewarm route table. Canary ran at 5% traffic for 48h.
- Results: median latency for payloads < 256B dropped from 84ms -> 56ms, p95 from 260ms -> 170ms, p99 from 320ms -> 210ms. Tokenized cost per request down ~9% due to reduced tail retries.
- Observed anomaly: 0.02% of requests hit stale mapping during metadata refresh windows which produced 500s; root cause: cache invalidation race when a pool reassign occurs mid-refresh.
- Decision: keep fast-path but add short-lived tombstone flag for recently-reassigned routes to avoid immediate reuse; patch merged in PR #892.
- Action: Marcus -> roll to 25% canary Tuesday morning (PLT-2345).

3) Quota fallback prototype (Elena)
- Purpose: provide deterministic degraded service behavior when quotas are saturated (avoid opaque 429s). Prototype behavior: if a route exceeds quota, route to lower-cost model variant with best-effort latency SLO, and emit structured telemetry.
- Simulation: ran replay against 72h weekend traces with spike scenarios; 93% of degraded cases served successfully with acceptable output; cost simulation shows ~12% unit-cost reduction for bursty workloads due to fewer hard rejects and better engine packing.
- Risks: degraded outputs could violate some strict enterprise SLAs. Need opt-in flag by customer and explicit contract language.
- Decision: move feature to opt-in beta behind account flag and include explicit audit log events.
- Action: Elena -> draft customer-facing beta brief + privacy/contract review (linked Confluence doc).

4) Auth token expiry regressions (Samir)
- Incident recap: Intermittent 401s observed for tokens rotated by the KMS pipeline; failures concentrated on edge proxies (region-eu-west-1) after rotation window.
- Root cause: edge proxy cache TTLs were longer than the auth service rotation propagation window; proxies continued using old verification keys for up to 9 minutes, while rotation expects 0-60s validity for rotated keys.
- Fix implemented: adjust proxy TTL to 30s and add keyset version header to forced refresh path. Hotfix deployed to edge cluster (canary 10 hosts) and verified.
- Remaining work: add end-to-end test in CI that simulates rotation and validates edge cache behavior.
- Actions: Samir -> create SEC ticket for formal postmortem (SEC-781); Priya -> add rotation test to integration pipeline.

5) Config schema validation (Priya)
- Problem: several routing outages this quarter traced to mismatched route config shapes (missing pool_id, malformed tags).
- Proposal: lift more validations into control plane pre-commit checks and CI step; add a lightweight JSON schema validator at deploy-time for control plane configs.
- Small spike results show ~70% of previously caught invalid files would be blocked earlier.
- Action: Priya -> prototyped validator, will open PR next week; add linter to infra repo and gate on merge.

6) Incident retrospective highlights
- The biggest blunder in the field sprint: manual bump-only deploys of routing metadata during the high-traffic window. We need a short deploy blackout and automated rollbacks for metadata changes during peak hours.
- Decision: enforce no-metadata-changes 11:00-18:00 PST unless via emergency runbook.
- Action: Aisha -> update runbook + notify Release Engineering.

7) Metrics snapshot (end of sprint)
- Avg qps across control plane: 4.8k (steady)
- Error rate (5m): 0.37% (mostly auth 401s prior to hotfix)
- Routing cache hit-rate: 96.2% (fast-path canary at 5%)
- Mean pod CPU (routing pool): 62%

8) Open questions / parking lot
- How do we present degraded-output guarantees to customers (UI/console and SLA language)? (Elena + Product)
- Should quorum for auth key rotation be extended to include edge replays? (Security/Infosec)
- Can we compress the tombstone window without increasing stale mapping risk? (Experiment)

9) Action items (owner, ticket/PR, due date)
- Marcus Liu: roll fast-path to 25% canary (PLT-2345) — due 2027-10-10
- Elena Rodriguez: beta brief + legal review for quota fallback — due 2027-10-14
- Samir Banerjee: write formal postmortem and link SEC ticket (SEC-781) — due 2027-10-08
- Priya Shah: open PR for config validator + CI gating — due 2027-10-12
- Aisha Patel: update deploy blackout policy + runbook entry — due 2027-10-07
- Alex Kim: add e2e rotation test in CI (collab w/ Samir) — due 2027-10-11

10) Notes to self / informal items
- Keep daily short check-ins during next canary ramp (10-15m async updates in #platform-controlplane Slack).
- Need to schedule a 1h cross-functional workshop (Product + Legal + Eng) to nail the beta contract language for quota fallback.

11) Next meeting: 2027-10-12 10:00 PT — sprint wrap + canary review.

Appendix: quick links and references
- Fast-path PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/892
- Canary plan ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLT-2345
- Quota fallback design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLT/Quota+Fallback+Design

-- end of notes (draft)
